ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023, -030, -035 thru -066
BLM’s Motion to Sever and Dismiss Group 1 Appeals
and Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Jurisdiction Denied
Now pending and fully briefed are BLM’s Motion to Sever and Dismiss Group 1
Appeals (Guerry Motion) and Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Jurisdiction (JRS Motion).
These motions pertain to two groups of grazing decisions: (1) decisions issued February
28, 2020 (Group 1) and decisions issued June 15, 2020 (Group 2). For the reasons set
forth below, those motions are denied.
The Guerry Motion seeks dismissal of Docket Nos. ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023,
and -030, which involve appeals by Western Watersheds Project (WWP) and WildLands
Defense (WLD) of February 28, 2020, grazing decisions issued to the grazing permittee,
Guerry, Inc., for the Coonskin-EJD and Pigtail Butte Allotments (Allotments). JRS
Properties III LLLP (JRS), another grazing permittee of the Allotments, was granted
intervenor party status in those cases.
The JRS Motion seeks dismissal of Docket Nos. ID-JFO-2020-043, -045, -048, -064,
and -066, which involve appeals by WWP, WLD, and JRS of June 15, 2020, grazing
decisions issued to JRS for the Allotments. JRS was granted intervenor party status in
the appeals of WWP and WLD.
JRS was granted intervenor party status in the appeals of the Group 1 decisions
affecting the Allotments (Docket Nos. ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023, and -030) by Order
dated September 3, 2020. That Order also consolidated the appeals of the Group 1
decisions and the Group 2 decisions affecting the Coonskin-EJD Allotment (Docket Nos.
ID-JFO-2020-006, -023, -043, -046, -064) and consolidated the Group 1 decisions and the
Group 2 decisions affecting the Pigtail Allotment (Docket Nos. ID-JFO-2020-013, -030,
-045, -048, -066).
For the appeals of the Cookskin-EJD Allotment decisions, that Order reasoned as
follows regarding consolidation and JRS’s intervention in the appeals of the Guerry
decision:
Given that both decisions establish a single integrated grazing
scheme with a single deferment schedule, single set of range
improvements, and single set of Objectives, Management Guidelines,
Thresholds, and Responses for a single allotment, there is great
commonality of facts pertinent to all appeals of the decisions. The
commonality of issues is also great, as all, or nearly all, the issues raised
13

ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023, -030, -035 thru -066
by WWP and WLD pertain to both decisions. Thus, consolidation of all
the Coonskin-EJD appeals is clearly warranted.
JRS’s intervention in the appeals relating to Guerry’s permit is also
warranted because, as a practical matter, JRS’s interests in grazing the
allotment would be impaired if a decision unfavorable to its positions
regarding the integrated grazing management scheme is entered in those
appeals. JRS’s positions include the assertion that this scheme established
in both decisions lacks a rational basis and will not work as intended, thus
harming JRS’s interests.
. . . .
In fact, because BLM has designed an integrated system of grazing
management for the allotment, DCHD would arguably be bound to issue
rulings regarding the decisions which are consistent, or it would
otherwise effectively implement a new, judge-made grazing decision
without the benefit of public input or BLM analysis and with potentially
unintentional adverse consequences to the environment or the permittees.
See WWP v. BLM, 195 IBLA 115, 123-24 (2020). Taking such action is not in
the public interest, see id. at 124, and amounts to managing the public
lands as a proxy for BLM, which DCHD does not have authority to do, S.
Utah Wilderness Alliance, 172 IBLA 183, 184-85 (2007).
These principles bolster the conclusion that the rulings to be made
regarding Guerry’s permit are inextricably linked to the rulings to be
made pertaining to JRS’s permit. Consequently, rulings regarding
Guerry’s permit may impair JRS’s interests and JRS’s intervention in the
appeals pertaining to Guerry’s permit for the Coonskin-EJD Allotment is
justified.
Sept. 3, 2020 Order at 8-9. For similar reasons, JRS was granted intervenor status in the
appeals of the Pigtail Butte Allotment decision issued to Guerry and the appeals
regarding the Pigtail Butte Allotment were consolidated.
Later, the appeals of the Group 1 decisions were consolidated and the appeals of
the Group 2 decisions were consolidated. All ten dockets pertaining to the Allotments
were consolidated with both the consolidated appeals pertaining to the Group 1
decisions and the consolidated appeals pertaining to the Group 2 decisions because
BLM’s stated rationale for the Group 1 decisions is not the same as its stated rationale
14

ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023, -030, -035 thru -066
for the Group 2 decisions, necessitating JRS’s involvement in both groups of appeals to
protect its interests for those ten dockets. See Orders dated March 17, 2021, and April
19, 2021.
Then, the parties filed cross-motions for summary judgment regarding the
appeals pertaining to the Group 1 decisions. In addressing briefing of the summary
judgment motions, this Tribunal declined to limit the briefing to specific issues.
By Orders dated August 9, 2021, this Tribunal granted summary judgment to
BLM regarding the consolidated appeals of the Group 1 decisions. Neither WWP nor
WLD appealed the order granting summary judgment against it.
In the Guerry Motion, BLM seeks (1) severance of the four dockets pertaining to
the Group 1 decisions affecting the Allotments (Docket Nos. ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -
023, and -030) from the consolidated Group 2 appeals and (2) dismissal of those four
dockets. BLM argues that the August 9, 2021 Orders granting summary judgment to
BLM on the WWP and WLD Group 1 appeals and the subsequent failure of WWP and
WLD to appeal those orders results in BLM’s Group 1 decisions becoming final. BLM
therefore requests that the appeals be severed from the Group 2 appeals and dismissed.
In the JRS Motion, BLM argues that the Tribunal lacks jurisdiction over the six
dockets pertaining to the Group 2 decisions affecting the Allotments (Docket Nos. ID-
JFO-2020-043, -045, -048, -064, and -066) because JRS limited its summary judgment
briefing for the appeals of the Group 1 decisions to certain issues, that BLM was granted
summary judgment on those issues in the August 9, 2021 Order, and that the Interior
Board of Land Appeals now has jurisdiction over the matters by virtue of JRS’s appeal
of the August 9, 2021 Order. BLM argues that “JRS Properties did not raise other issues
that it could have in its Group 1 briefs, and it may not unilaterally do what the Hearings
Division declined to do, which is limit the issues to be litigated [in the Group 1]
proceeding, while reserving the right to maintain arguments for another day [in the
Group 2 proceeding].”
JRS persuasively argues that both motions should be denied:
. . . BLM’s Guerry Motion should be denied because JRS has party status
via its intervenor status in such four (4) dockets and JRS remains to have
such party status to further adjudicate such dockets in the above-noted
JFO Group 2 dockets (which is currently subject to a cross-motion for
summary judgment process).
15

ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023, -030, -035 thru -066
And, BLM’s Guerry Motion and BLM’s JRS Motion should be
denied because the Hearings Division decided in the ALJ Orders dated
March 17, 2021 and April 19, 2021, to consolidate and to have concurrent
jurisdiction over such ten (10) dockets relative to the Hearings Division
adjudication of such dockets in JFO Group 1 and in JFO Group 2.1
Assuming, however, the Hearings Division (now) finds that it cannot have
concurrent jurisdiction over the six (6) docket numbers subject to BLM’s
JRS Motion, then the Hearings Division should issue an Order -- either
directing the BLM / JRS to move the Board or requesting the Board on its
own Order -- to suspend the Board’s jurisdiction over IBLA-2021-0335
pending the Hearings Division’s concurrent jurisdiction and adjudication
of JFO Group 2 dockets as to such six (6) docket numbers so the currently
pending JFO Group 2 summary judgment motion process and
adjudication process can continue and not be delayed as to, at least, the
ten (10) dockets at issue.
“RESPONSE BY JRS PROPERTIES III LLLP TO (1) BLM’s ‘Motion to Sever and Dismiss
Group 1 Appeals Pertaining to the Coonskin-EJD and Pigtail Butte Allotments’ dated
October 12, 2021, and (2) BLM’s ‘Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Jurisdiction’ dated
October 12, 2021” at 4-5.
In other words, JRS did not lose its party status in the four dockets pertaining to
the Group 1 decisions when WWP and WLD chose not to appeal the orders granting
summary judgment and the four dockets remain active with respect to JRS’s
contentions as part of the Group 2 appeals. The four dockets were consolidated with
both the Group 1 consolidated appeals and the Group 2 consolidated appeals. The
Group 2 appeals and JRS’s contentions remain pending regarding the integrated
grazing scheme approved in both the four Group 1 dockets and the six Group 2 dockets
pertaining to the Allotments. THEREFORE, THE GUERRY MOTION IS DENIED.
Regarding the JRS Motion, BLM elaborates on its argument:
Management on the ground with respect to the JRS Properties
decisions is currently stayed based on a stipulation BLM agreed to at the
onset of the appeals before the Hearings Division. However, that stay
does not extend past the issuance of a final order resolving the appeal at
the Hearings Division. After that, a party must file a new petition for stay
at the IBLA or enter into a new stipulation with BLM. The practical
consequence of having an appeal in two tribunals is that BLM is not sure
whether it is constrained by the stipulation with respect to the appeals
16

ID-JFO-2020-006, -013, -023, -030, -035 thru -066
before the Hearings Division, or if it has the right to decide whether to
stipulate to a new stay in the IBLA proceedings, or oppose a stay petition.
This uncertainty is resolved by recognizing the body that has jurisdiction
over the entirety of the appeals pertaining to the JRS Properties decisions
for the Coonskin-EJD and Pigtail Butte allotments—IBLA.
JRS Motion at 3-4.
The simple answer to this argument is that the six Group 2 dockets were
consolidated with both the Group 1 appeals and the Group 2 appeals, so they remain
pending before this Tribunal as part of the Group 2 consolidated appeals and this
Tribunal has jurisdiction over them. What course of action BLM may choose before the
IBLA is not at issue in this proceeding. THEREFORE, THE JRS MOTION IS DENIED.
Acting First Judge Supervisory
